description: Fideo Seco is a comforting Mexican dish featuring toasted pasta simmered in a rich, flavorful tomato sauce until tender. This beloved dry noodle dish captures the heart of Mexican home cooking, offering a delightful blend of textures and savory notes. It is a simple yet incredibly satisfying meal, perfect for a family dinner.

instructions.title: Prepare the Tomato Sauce Base
instructions.text: In a blender, combine the roughly chopped Roma tomatoes, quartered white onion, peeled garlic cloves, chicken broth, salt, and ground cumin. Blend until the mixture is completely smooth. Set aside.

instructions.title: Toast the Fideo Noodles
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the fideo noodles and cook, stirring constantly, until they are golden brown and toasted. This step is crucial for flavor and texture. Be careful not to burn them.

instructions.title: Add the Tomato Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully pour the blended tomato sauce over the toasted fideo noodles in the skillet. The mixture will sizzle. Stir well to ensure all the noodles are coated with the sauce.

instructions.title: Simmer and Cook
instructions.text: Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Once simmering, reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and let it cook for 15-20 minutes, or until the noodles are tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Rest and Fluff
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the skillet from the heat and let the fideo seco rest, covered, for 5 minutes. This allows the remaining liquid to be fully absorbed and the flavors to meld. After resting, gently fluff the noodles with a fork.

instructions.title: Serve with Toppings
instructions.text: Serve the Fideo Seco immediately. Garnish each serving generously with a drizzle of Crema Mexicana, crumbled queso fresco, slices of fresh avocado, and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro. Enjoy this authentic Mexican comfort food.

tips: Do not skip the toasting of the fideo noodles. This step gives the dish its characteristic nutty flavor and prevents the noodles from becoming mushy.
For a spicier kick, add one or two serrano or jalapeño peppers to the blender with the tomatoes and other sauce ingredients.
Fideo Seco is excellent as a main course or a side dish. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheated gently on the stovetop or in the microwave.
